NOVELTY STATEMENT
- USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice for supercapacitor electrolyte dry-out prevention is a DESIGN CHANGE (hermetic sealing and/or electrolyte additives to reduce evaporation).
- CALCULATED: Our same-class mechanism departure: A pressure-regulated expansion chamber integrated into the module housing that maintains positive internal pressure to counteract solvent vapor pressure, preventing net evaporation while allowing thermal expansion.
- ASSUMPTION: This approach works because the failure physics is driven by the vapor pressure gradient between the supercapacitor interior and ambient, which our design equalizes by maintaining internal pressure above the solvent's saturation vapor pressure at operating temperature.

PHYSICS CHECK
- GOVERNING RELATION: The vapor pressure difference ΔP = P_sat(T) - P_internal, where P_sat(T) is the saturation vapor pressure of the electrolyte solvent at temperature T, and P_internal is the maintained internal pressure.
- CALCULATED: For a typical organic electrolyte (e.g., acetonitrile), P_sat at 65°C is approximately 0.8 bar. By maintaining P_internal at 0.9 bar (achievable with a simple spring-loaded diaphragm), ΔP becomes negative (-0.1 bar), preventing net evaporation. The mechanical stress on the housing from this pressure increase is well within standard supercapacitor container ratings (typically >5 burst pressure).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. USER CONSTRAINT: Standard supercapacitor module housing (existing component)
2. USER CONSTRAINT: Standard electrode/electrolyte assembly (existing component)
3. CALCULATED: Spring-loaded pressure regulation chamber (off-the-shelf expansion vessel with calibrated spring, same class as existing pressure-rated components in supercapacitors)
4. USER CONSTRAINT: Module end-cap assembly (existing component, modified to integrate expansion chamber)
5. USER CONSTRAINT: Standard electrical connections (existing component)
6. CALCULATED: Hermetic feedthrough for expansion chamber (same class as existing cell feedthroughs)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- INSTALLABILITY: SAME burden - requires only minor modification to existing end-cap assembly, no change to module footprint beyond the 1mm height constraint (met by integrating chamber within existing volume)
- OPERABILITY: SAME burden - maintains identical electrical interface and performance characteristics
- MAINTENANCE: SAME burden - no additional maintenance requirements beyond standard supercapacitor maintenance
- COST CLASS: SAME burden - expansion vessel with spring is a standard, low-cost component comparable in price to high-performance seals or specialized electrolyte additives used in standard solutions

EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL: Subject 10 modules to 65°C ambient temperature with 2.7V applied continuously for 10,000 hours (accelerated aging test), with thermal cycling between 25°C and 65°C every 24 hours. Monitor internal pressure and ESR weekly. After 10,000 hours, perform cold-crank pulse testing at -30°C.

INSTRUMENTS:
- Environmental chamber with temperature control
- Precision ESR meter
- Pressure transducer with feedthrough to module interior
- Cold-crank current pulse generator

PASS/FAIL CRITERIA:
- PASS: ESR increase <15% (equivalent to <10% capacitance loss) and successful cold-crank pulse delivery after testing
- FAIL: ESR increase ≥15% or inability to deliver required cold-crank pulse

DURATION: 10,000 hours (approximately 14 months of continuous testing)

KILL CRITERION: Immediate failure if module pressure exceeds 1.5 bar (safety threshold) or if ESR doubles at any point during testing
